findings: Source is BT Group plc Annual Report 2026 (Companies House consolidated group accounts, FY ended 31 March 2026); Strategic report approved by the Board 20 May 2026 and signed by Chairman Adam Crozier (docs/data/research_director_worker/BT-A.L/20260904T201714Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_04190816_MzUzNTE1NzIyNWFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Extract covers only front matter, Chairman/CEO letters, Executive Committee and opening business-model pages (~1,081 lines); Group performance (p.46), financial statements (from p.120), segment notes, balance sheet and pension note are not present in this body file.

Contents-page headline KPIs (OCR-degraded): group revenue FY26 ~£19.7bn vs FY25 £20.4bn; profit before tax FY26 ~£1.4bn (+8%) vs FY25 £1.3bn; adjusted EBITDA FY26 ~£8.2bn vs FY25 £8.2bn (docs/data/research_director_worker/BT-A.L/20260904T201714Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_04190816_MzUzNTE1NzIyNWFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Clear FY26 vs FY25 group metrics on contents summary: cashflow from operating activities £7.0bn (+1%, FY25 £7.0bn); normalised free cash flow £1.5bn (−6%, FY25 £1.6bn); basic EPS 11.0p (+2%, FY25 10.8p); capital expenditure £5.1bn (+6%, FY25 £4.9bn) (same source).

Adjusted EBITDA defined as group profit or loss before specific items, net finance expense, taxation, depreciation and amortisation and share of post-tax profits/losses of associates and joint ventures; normalised FCF definition referenced to p.226 (not included in extract) (same source).

Board proposed increased full-year dividend of 8.32p per share for FY26; from FY27 new dividend policy to increase DPS by a low single-digit percentage annually until metrics consistent with BBB+ credit rating, then deploy residual cash flow to enhanced shareholder distributions while meeting pension-fund commitments (same source).

FY27/outlook language: reiterates cash-flow inflection to ~£2bn in FY27 rising to ~£3bn by end of decade; plans full fibre to 30m UK homes/businesses (beyond 25m premises target by end-2026) and 5G+ to 99% of population by Spring 2030 (same source).
Openreach operational (no revenue split): full fibre passes 23m homes/businesses (>two-thirds of UK) with 8.8m+ connected; record FY26 build/connections (same source).
EE/mobile operational: 5G+ at 73% of population; 5G footprint 90.5%; EE awarded best UK mobile network in three separate awards (same source).
Consumer division grew customer numbers across mobile, broadband and TV for first time in eight years; >50% of broadband customers on full fibre; multi-service homes 27% (same source).

Transformation programme delivering ahead of plan: target raised to £3.7bn gross savings (from £3.0bn), extended one year to FY30; completed all non-core international divestments (five businesses sold) and carved out BT International (same source).

Regulatory/stakeholder: cites 2025 Budget, Mobile Market Review and Statement of Strategic Priorities; welcomes Chancellor support for fibre to 30m premises and 5G+ to 99%; Ofcom Telecoms Access Review cited as providing sector clarity; open regulator relationship emphasised (same source).
CEO states FY26 delivered on financial guidance and, adjusting for divestments, EBITDA grew, keeping group on track for promised cash-flow inflection (same source).

No segment revenue (Openreach vs Consumer/EE vs Business/Global), statutory operating profit/EPS, balance-sheet debt/lease/net-debt, BTPS funding, buyback cash, specific-item/restructuring charges, or fibre-vs-other capex split appear in this extract.
